history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed (Buddhist sacred complex, not a monastery or temple building; the CSV name 'Buddha Park Temple' is a misnomer — it is a park). Tathagata Tsal was constructed 2006–2013 to mark the 2550th anniversary of the birth of Gautama Buddha; its 130-ft (40 m) copper statue (repoussage, 60 tonnes) was consecrated by the 14th Dalai Lama on 25 March 2013, with Mount Narsing as backdrop. The site lies within the religious complex of the Rabong (Rabongla) Monastery; the complex also holds a Buddhist conclave, meditation centre, museum with spiral gallery, and Cho Djo lake.

town_description: Ravangla (Rabong) is a small hill town in South Sikkim at the base of Maenam Hill, a transit point for treks to Maenam and Borong and for the Rangit valley hot springs, now a pilgrimage-tourism hub on the Himalayan Buddhist Circuit.

travel.road: ~1 km north of Ravangla town; SNT buses and private/shared taxis run from Ravangla to Siliguri and towns within Sikkim
